Marathon Petroleum fell nearly 0.08% today, extending a sharp two-week decline of 10.65%, as crude oil prices tumbled on optimism over Iran conflict resolution. Brent crude dipped below $90 per barrel for the first time since August after President Trump suggested the conflict would end "fairly soon"—a major shift for refiners like MPC, whose profits depend on the spread between crude input costs and refined product prices. Lower crude prices narrow that margin, which helps their bottom line theoretically, but markets appear to be pricing in a longer-term risk: sustained lower oil prices reduce the premium refiners earn.

The broader headwind is a political one. Recent midterm elections dealt a blow to anti-renewable policies, signaling growing investor appetite for cleaner energy. For a refiner whose business model centers on processing crude into gasoline and diesel, a structural shift toward renewables and electric vehicles represents a slower but more persistent threat than any single day's oil price move.
